_readme: data/wave-grids.json - the committed IDENTITY expectation for the three NOAA GRIB2 wave
grids, read by scripts/build-wave-manifest.js as the gridIdentity and bandIdentity gates
before any cycle is published.
WHY IT IS DUPLICATED. Every number here also appears in GRIDS in src/waveGrids.js. That is
deliberate, and it is the same split scripts/clip-layers.js and scripts/build-manifest.js
already use: src/waveGrids.js is the PRODUCER (it drives the fetch and the sampler) and this
file is the GATE's expectation. A gate that imported its expectations from the thing it gates
would be checking the producer against itself, which proves nothing. Both copies move
together, in one reviewed commit.
WHAT IT CATCHES. A grid whose decoded raster no longer matches its committed size,
geotransform, cell size or nodata is a grid whose cell indices mean something different than
the sampler assumes. Upstream changing a domain, GDAL changing a warp default, or a shell
argument being edited all produce a raster that decodes cleanly, samples without error, and
returns wave heights from the wrong place on earth. There is no other signal for that.
sampled{} describes the raster handed to scripts/sample-waves.js, AFTER the workflow's
gdal_translate (noaa_gfswave, already lat/lon) or gdalwarp (noaa_glwu and noaa_gfswave_arctic,
both projected). nodata is the value GDAL reports in the band header for that grid; it is
compared, never assumed, because gfswave uses 9999 and GLWU uses 9.999000260554009e+20 and a
hardcoded 9999 would pass every Great Lakes sentinel into a flag color.
bands[] is the GRIB_ELEMENT set every sampled band must be drawn from, asserted per band
index against gdalinfo -json. HTSGW is metres and WIND is metres per second; there is no GUST
element in gfswave, which is why windGustMph is permanently null on this pipeline.
tolerance{} is the absolute epsilon the gate compares geotransform floats within. It is not a
licence to drift: it exists because a warp origin is a float and an exact equality test on
floats is a gate that fails for the wrong reason. nodata is compared RELATIVELY instead, via
NODATA_MATCH_RELATIVE in src/waveGrids.js: gdalinfo -json prints a large nodata with about
eight significant digits, so GLWU's sentinel reads back slightly rounded and an equality test
would refuse every cycle over a formatting difference.
